## 2026-08-02 14:01 UTC-05:00 · round-close · corpus/frontface-ocr
Vision pass on the 21 held hyphens: 4 were OCR misreads disguised as compounds (provide/fluorine/dilute/pastries) — all 4 in the KEEP bucket, exactly as predicted. Applied 29 edits over 21 claims, sealed at knowledge_version=440; front-facing split words 180 → 1.
  ↳ We held back 21 word-splits during the hyphen pass because they looked like real compound words — things you'd never want joined, like "acetyl-CoA" or "whooping-cough". This pass opened the actual book pages and checked every one. Four of them were not compounds at all: they were OCR misreads wearing a compound's costume. The news clipping you first complained about is now byte-correct against its page, and across the whole corpus the count of broken-looking split words went from 180 this morning to 1 — and that last one is a different kind of defect, left on purpose and named below. ★ THE FINDING, and it was predicted in writing. All four OCR errors were in the "KEEP — real compound" bucket. Phase 1a's own notes said why this had to happen: JOIN is POSITIVE evidence ("the rejoined token IS a real word"), while KEEP is NEGATIVE evidence ("it isn't") and is therefore only as good as its input. If OCR corrupted one half, the rejoin cannot produce a word, so the pair lands in KEEP and looks exactly like a compound. Against the pages: RARE-000336 pro-|side is pro-vide (provide); RARE-000365 fluo-|tine is fluo-rine (fluorine); RARE-000389 di-|Jute is di-lute (dilute); RARE-000400 past-|ties is past-ries (pastries). Every one is a single-letter misread of the SECOND half — v→s, r→t, l→J, r→t — and every one yields a real English word in a plausible position, so no mechanical check could ever have found them. That is the entire argument for a vision pass, demonstrated on a 4-for-18 hit rate. WHAT WAS APPLIED — 29 edits across 21 claims. - 15 de-newline, KEEP the hyphen: the wrap fell ON a real compound hyphen, so the hyphen was correct but the line break still rendered as "anti- inflammatory" with a space (anti-inflammatory, iron-containing, whooping-cough, by-products, Twenty-two, acid-deficient, anti-psoriatic, genetically-transmitted, myo-inositol, low-sodium, drinking-water, eosinophilia-myalgia, OH-group, acetyl-CoA, Wernicke-Korsakoff). - 2 full joins: pre-mature → premature, co-las → colas. Both had been wrongly KEPT because book_purity's CHEM_PREFIX rule fires on the ordinary English prefixes "pre-" and "co-" and outranked the rejoined-is-a-word test. That rule ordering is a real bug and is recorded for the next pass. - 4 OCR-fix-then-join (the four above). - 6 MORE Phase-0-verified defects inside RARE-000336 (f→of, tisk→risk, rea→area, the missing "the" before National Cancer Institute, he→the, ancer→cancer) and 2 inside EPIGEN-000239 (the subscript B, → B1, matching the book's own B1 convention; and surgeon, → surgeon.). These were vision-verified during Phase 0 and left unapplied. Fixing only the hyphen in RARE-000336 would have left "tisk", "rea" and "ancer" on screen in the exact quote he reported — memory fix-as-found-never-defer. NOT FIXED, and named rather than quietly skipped. LETS-000512 Pharma-|Need is not a hyphen problem at all. The page is a TABLE whose headers read Nutrient | RDA | True Supplement Need | 30-Day Pharmacologic Daily Dose. The OCR read ACROSS columns, splicing "Pharma-" (from "Pharmacologic", broken inside its own column) onto "Need" from the neighbouring column. It needs a table-structure correction, not a rejoin, so it is the single remaining split in the sealed corpus and it is deliberate. ★ A PHASE-1 BLOCKER SURFACED. ## 2026-08-02 13:38 UTC-05:00 · round-close · corpus/frontface-ocr
Phase 1a: rejoined 155 typesetter line-break hyphens in front-facing quotes (180 -> 22, every remainder a named hold), sealed at knowledge_version=439 — after catching and fixing a corpus_resnap defect that silently trimmed 69 verbatims past every green gate.
  ↳ Some quotes in the app were showing words broken in half — "try- ing", "de- spite", "mal- absorption". That was never an OCR error: the book's typesetter split those words across a line, our text copied the page faithfully, and the app collapses the line break so the leftover hyphen ends up mid-word on screen. 155 of them are now rejoined in the source, so every surface shows whole words. Along the way a bug in one of our own tools was caught that would have quietly damaged 69 quotes, and it was fixed before anything was sealed. SCOPE. The mandate is front-facing quotes only, never whole-book. 180 line-break hyphens sit inside 91 front-facing verbatims. Classified 159 JOIN / 18 KEEP / 3 REVIEW; applied 155 edit sites (158 occurrences — 3 passages are each quoted by two claims, so they collapse to one physical site) across rare-earths 106, lets-play-doctor 48, epigenetics 1, immortality 0. Remaining in the sealed corpus afterwards: 22 occurrences in 21 quotes — EXACTLY the named holds, so nothing was silently dropped. THE DISCRIMINATOR, and why it is not book_purity's. book_purity asks "are BOTH halves real words?" and reviews if so. Correct for a whole-book sweep, wrong here: it sends de-|spite and mal-|absorption to review because de, mal, spite and absorption are all words, when the answers are obviously despite and malabsorption. The sharper question for a LINE-BREAK wrap is whether the REJOINED token is itself a real word: try+ing -> trying joins; potassium+rich -> potassiumrich does not. book_purity's two hard KEEP rules (chemical/stereo prefix, proper-noun second half) were inherited unchanged and override the join. WHY THIS WAS SAFE TO DO BEFORE THE VISION PASS. De-hyphenation is orthogonal to OCR correctness — it removes a typesetting artifact and cannot create, hide or worsen a letter error. It is also self-protecting: if OCR corrupted either half, the rejoin almost never yields a real word, so it lands in KEEP/REVIEW rather than JOIN. The converse is the load-bearing caveat: a KEEP verdict is NEGATIVE evidence and is only as good as its input. WAL-CLM-RARE-000336's pro-|side was ruled "a real compound" purely because the page's "vide" had been OCR'd to "side" — it is not a compound, the page says provide. So all 21 KEEP/REVIEW cases wait for vision, and the hyphen pass MUST be re-run afterwards, at which point pro-|vide reclassifies to JOIN by itself. HELD BY NAME (never a silent skip). 18 KEEP — real compounds (Twenty-two, acid-deficient, low-sodium, drinking-water, OH-group, iron-containing, whooping-cough), chemical prefixes (anti-psoriatic, anti-inflammatory, pre-mature, co-las) and proper nouns (acetyl-CoA, Wernicke-Korsakoff, Pharma-Need, di-Jute). 3 REVIEW, all ratified by Luneth: fluo-|tine is almost certainly fluo-rine with an OCR r->t (vision must confirm); myo-inositol and eosinophilia-myalgia are the standard hyphenated forms and keep their hyphen. 1 style-hold: by-products, Luneth's call — both spellings are valid, byproducts is in the dictionary so the rule joined it, and no machine rule separates that class. ★ THE TOOL DEFECT, FOUND AND FIXED BEFORE SEALING. The first corpus_resnap run trimmed 69 of the 77 healed verbatims. relocate()'s HEAL path anchors on the letters-only skeleton and spanned first-alphanumeric..last-alphanumeric, so a verbatim's leading or trailing NON-alphanumeric run fell outside the anchor: 68 lost a closing . " or ), WAL-CLM-RARE-000342 lost all four of its !!!!, and four gained a stray leading letter. NOTHING WOULD HAVE CAUGHT IT. The trimmed text is still a byte-exact substring of the source — just the wrong span — so corpus_verify check #2, check #9 and all 81 gates stay green on a quote that now ends mid-punctuation in the reader's face. My own audit was blind to it BY CONSTRUCTION: it compared letters-only skeletons, and the lost characters are not letters. It surfaced only because I spot-checked WAL-CLM-LETS-000502 by eye and noticed its closing !!) had vanished. That is the whole lesson: the instrument and the check shared a blind spot, and the eye broke the tie (memory: the-instrument-lies-before-the-eye, negative-control-or-it-proves-nothing). Fixed at the tool rather than the 69 symptoms (§00.B: fix systemically). relocate() now re-attaches the ORIGINAL verbatim's own leading/trailing runs, and ONLY where the corrected book text actually still carries them, so it restores the true span and never invents one. Shipped in the same patch with tools/test_corpus_resnap_edges.py — 6 cases: the load-bearing trailing period (the shape of all 68), a multi-character !!!! run, a leading quote, plus three SPARING cases (an absent edge is not invented, the exact-match path stays byte-identical, genuinely missing text is still BROKEN) — and a negative control proving the test fails against the pre-fix code. After the fix: 0 trimmed. The 7 claims whose length delta still differs from their join count all shrank LESS than expected with identical tails, which is exactly the held KEEP/style cases. PROCESS. Text edits computed in LF space (books-meta records hash_basis=lf_normalized_utf8 and every char_offset indexes the LF-normalized text, while the .txt files are CRLF on disk); safe_write's text-mode write lands LF payloads as CRLF, verified empirically on a throwaway probe rather than assumed. Validate-ALL-then-write: every edit site re-verified against live bytes, one mismatch would have aborted the run before a single file was staged. Drafts re-synced from the resnapped shards and corpus_seal's own draft_offset_failures() run as proof BEFORE sealing (0 failures) — that guard exists because resnap fixes the shard only and promotion would otherwise restore stale offsets. VERIFIED. corpus_seal -> knowledge_version=439, corpus_verify PASS (2268 claims, 7 books, hashes match). No §00.A exposure: zero overlap between the 77 changed claims and the 38 dose-target source_claim_ids in essentials-targets-data.json. Board 81/81 after build_embeds + build. render_probe_knowledge, render_probe_search and render_probe_entity all PASS with 0 page errors. The shipped dist/main.js carries "been trying for a pregnancy", "of normal despite supplementation", "case of malabsorption" and "A pregnancy!!)", and none of the stale splits. DEFERRED. MEASURED BEFORE TOUCHING ANYTHING. Every sample was the ordinary-English sense ("Germanium deficiency is typified by a severely reduced immune status", "a reduction in inflammation markers", "the reduction or absence of acid in the stomach"). Zero chemistry-sense firings. 129 wrong tooltips, 0 right ones. SCOPE DECISION, stated rather than assumed. The reported word was "reduced". Removing only that alias would have left "reduction" over-firing 24x; removing both aliases leaves an entry that can never fire. So the whole entry was deleted — dashboard/assets/data/glossary.json, 1246 -> 1245 definitions (hand-authored R4 prose store, MANIFEST-allowlisted, §17 safe_write). New critical invariant `glossary_keys_denylisted` (tools/invariants.py) re-implements the runtime normalization exactly (lower-case, curly apostrophes folded, [\s-] runs collapsed to one space) and matches on key EQUALITY, never containment — so "oxidation-reduction" and a hypothetical "reduced glutathione" are spared by construction, and only the bare common word is closed. Denylisting the morphological family follows the R9 lesson already recorded on term_gloss_ratified_present: a literal key match misses near-variants. A denylist entry with no recorded reason is itself RED, so a future removal cannot be slipped in unreviewed. WHY THIS GATE AND NOT A SMARTER ONE (R7, labeled honestly). It closes the door behind a key a human has judged and removed. It does NOT discover the next over-firing common word, and I did not pretend otherwise: there is no non-gaming machine test for "is this key a common English word", and a frequency floor is actively wrong here — the same scan shows 'essential' firing 627x, 'trace' 257x, 'isolated' 154x and 'chronic' 137x, all deliberate.
